newsitem.title: USA: Clinton Administration rejects DC school package.
newsitem.headline: Clinton Administration rejects DC school package.

text.p: The Clinton Administration is opposed to a request for $52.4 million in federal funds to make emergency repairs to Washington's public schools and give its police officers a 10 percent raise, the Washington Post reported Thursday.

Federal Budget Director Franklin D. Raines said in a letter to D.C. financial control board chairman Andrew F. Brimmer that the control board instead should squeeze the funds out of the District's $5 billion budget, the Post reported.
Raines also said the control board failed to explain how its short-term funding request fit in with a comprehensive White House plan to revitalize the District.

The Post reported that Brimmer was disappointed by the White House response and would continue to press for more money. Brimmer said that the control board already has "scrubbed" the D.C. budget and that there is no room for fresh cuts to provide funds for the school system and the police force.
DC officials could not be reached for immediate comment.
